text: Auto-ships keep pets on their medicine without a phone call. When a family calls about one, walk them through the same window they see.
In Maria's portal, she picks Maple.
Maple's heartworm chewable is on auto-ship. See the tag.
Manage opens it.
Here's when it ships next, and what it costs.
She can change how often,
or how many come in each shipment,
or move the next date. It has to be at least two days out, because we bill and pack on that day.
She can pause it for a while,
or cancel it.
And she can order one extra right now.
Done closes the window.
If her card is declined, she sees this red banner: payment failing.
Payment failing means one thing: she updates her card here. Nothing else fixes it.
Update card.
She enters the new card right here, for this auto-ship.
In the store, Auto-ship at the top lists all of her auto-ships.
Each one can be changed, paused or cancelled here too.
The most common mistakes: cancelling an auto-ship because the card failed, and taking a new card number over the phone instead of having the client update it.
Remember: payment failing means the client updates the card in the portal. Nothing else fixes it.
